fact.title: One of the busiest websites on Earth is an adult video site.
fact.desc: It reported about 115 million visits a day in 2019, and in 2018 it sent 4,403 petabytes of video: about 140 GB every second, busiest late at night. Here is how a site like that stays up.
points: Each video is split into pieces a few seconds long, in several qualities. Any server can send any piece, and a player can switch quality between pieces when the network slows.
The CDN does the heavy lifting
Servers in hundreds of cities keep the popular pieces close to viewers. Almost every request ends there; the company's own servers see a small share.
Plan for the peak, not the average
Traffic is far higher at night than in the afternoon. Capacity is sized for the busiest hour, and the CDN absorbs the surges.
fact.source: Figures from the site's own published yearly reports for 2018 and 2019.

landingLab.title: Can your design survive IND vs PAK?
landingLab.desc: On 14 October 2023, 3.5 crore people watched India play Pakistan live on one streaming app, all at the same time. Here is the real Lab with that match loaded. Add what's missing, press Score, and see if the stream holds from the toss to the last over.
landingLab.note: Peak of 3.5 crore people watching at once: ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023, India vs Pakistan, as reported by the broadcaster. The app here is made up. Each player fetches a 4-second chunk every 4 seconds; capacities and prices are rules of thumb.

privacy.title: What is kept when you sign in
sections: Articles, notes and the full Lab on the dashboard work without an account. The IND vs PAK challenge on the home page asks you to sign in first. Without an account, your Lab designs and challenge stars stay in this browser's storage and nowhere else.

When you sign in with Google: your Google account ID, name (first and last), email address, the link to your profile picture, the country you signed in from, and when you signed in. Your Lab designs and challenge stars, so they follow you to other devices. Whether you agreed to see Tech Katta updates on Facebook and Instagram, and when. Your Google password is never seen by this site.

In a MongoDB Atlas database used only by this site. You stay signed in with a random token in a cookie that only the site's API can read; it ends when you sign out, after 30 days without a visit, or 90 days after you signed in. "Sign out on all devices" ends it everywhere at once.

To learn which articles and Lab challenges help, the site records what you do on it: pages and articles you open, how far you read, components you add, runs, scores, and signing in or out. Each browser gets a random ID kept in its own storage, not a cookie. When you're signed in, these records are linked to your account. They stay in the same database, are never shared, and are deleted after 13 months. If your browser asks sites not to track you (Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track), nothing is recorded.

Only if you tick "Show me Tech Katta updates on Facebook and Instagram" (it is never ticked for you). Then your email, name and country are hashed and uploaded to Meta to show you Tech Katta ads. The full details are in the Terms and conditions. You can turn it off any time in the account menu.
What is not done with it
No selling your data, no tracking cookies, nothing sent to analytics companies. Your email is not used to email you.

Use Delete my account in the account menu. Your account, designs, stars and the usage records linked to it are removed from the database straight away. The copy in your own browser stays until you clear it.

terms.title: Terms and conditions
sections: Tech Katta is free to use for learning system design. The articles, figures and Lab are explanations, not professional advice; the Lab's prices and numbers are estimates. Please don't overload the site, copy it wholesale, or try to break into it.
You sign in with Google. You can sign out, sign out on all devices, or delete your account at any time from the account menu. An account used to abuse the site can be closed.
Designs you make in the Lab are yours. They are kept in your account only so they show up on every device you use.

This applies only if you tick "Show me Tech Katta updates on Facebook and Instagram" when you sign in, or turn it on later in the account menu. It is never ticked for you, and you can use everything on the site without it. If you tick it, your email address, first and last name and country are turned into codes (SHA-256 hashes) and uploaded to Meta from time to time, so Meta can show Tech Katta ads to you on Facebook and Instagram, and to people with similar interests. Meta matches the codes against its own accounts. It does not get your designs, your stars or what you do on this site. You can turn it off any time in the account menu; you are then left out of the next upload, and you can ask Meta to forget you in your Facebook or Instagram ad settings.
What the site records about how it is used, and how long it is kept, is in the Privacy policy.
If these terms change, the date at the top changes too. Anything that affects the Facebook and Instagram updates will ask you again.
